guide.title: The Kumano Kodo Nakahechi from Takijiri-oji to Nachi Falls
guide.author: friends of Placemoir
guide.summary: The classic pilgrim trail through the Kii mountains: three or four walking days from Takijiri-oji to Kumano Hongu Taisha, then hot spring villages, Shingu and the falls at Nachi, with an inn at each stop.

places.name: Tanabe Tourist Information Center
places.notes: Right beside Kii-Tanabe Station, where the buses to Takijiri leave. Pick up trail maps and timetables here. Village lodging and luggage transfer fill early in spring and fall, so book well ahead through the Tanabe City Kumano Tourism Bureau.
places.section: Tanabe · Gateway town on the coast

places.name: Tokei-jinja Shrine
places.notes: An old branch of Hongu where pilgrims once prayed before heading into the mountains, set in a grove a short walk from the station. A good first stop to get the feel of a Kumano shrine before the trail.
places.section: Tanabe · Gateway town on the coast

places.name: Miyoshiya Ryokan
places.notes: A plain, friendly family ryokan a few minutes from Kii-Tanabe Station, set up for walkers catching the early bus to Takijiri. Tatami rooms, shared baths and the Ajikoji bar lanes close by for dinner.
places.section: Tanabe · Gateway town on the coast

places.name: Tsuji-no-Mochi
places.notes: A long-running sweets shop known for soft mochi topped with a stripe of red bean paste. Pick up a few as trail snacks for the first day.
places.section: Tanabe · Gateway town on the coast

places.name: Kumano Kodo Kan Pilgrimage Center
places.notes: The octagonal visitor center at the Takijiri bus stop, a few steps from the shrine. Look at the exhibits on the old pilgrimage, use the toilets and fill your water bottles before the steep climb.
places.section: Day 1 · Takijiri-oji to Takahara · about 4 km

places.name: Takijiri-oji
places.notes: The traditional entrance to the sacred mountains of Kumano, where two rivers meet. Stamp your pilgrim credential here, then start straight up the stone steps behind the shrine; the first hour is the steepest of the day.
places.section: Day 1 · Takijiri-oji to Takahara · about 4 km

places.name: Takahara Kumano-jinja
places.notes: One of the oldest shrine buildings on the route, painted in faded colors and shaded by huge camphor trees. It sits right on the trail as you enter Takahara.
places.section: Day 1 · Takijiri-oji to Takahara · about 4 km

places.name: Kiri-no-Sato Takahara Lodge
places.address: 霧の郷たかはら, 826, Nakahechicho Takahara, Tanabe, Wakayama, Japan 646-1416, 30 m, name 0.75, at 33.7962,135.5323); Takahara Kirinosato (Nakahechichotakahara, Tanabe-Shi, Wakayama, Japan 646-1416
places.notes: A wooden ridge-top lodge with wide views over the Hatenashi range, where morning mist often fills the valley below. Meals lean on local produce; book early through the Tanabe City Kumano Tourism Bureau.
places.section: Day 1 · Takijiri-oji to Takahara · about 4 km

places.name: Jujo-oji
places.notes: A rebuilt oji in the cedar forest roughly halfway through the day, with a rest hut and toilets nearby. There are no shops between Takahara and Chikatsuyu, so carry lunch and water.
places.section: Day 2 · Takahara to Chikatsuyu · about 10 km

places.name: Gyuba-doji Statue
places.address: Kumano Kodo, Chikatsuyu, Nakahechi-cho, Tanabe, Wakayama 646-1402
places.notes: A tiny stone figure riding a horse and an ox, said to recall the retired emperor Kazan on his pilgrimage. From here it is a short descent into Chikatsuyu.
places.section: Day 2 · Takahara to Chikatsuyu · about 10 km

places.name: Chikatsuyu-oji
places.notes: The oji where pilgrims purified themselves in the Hiki River before the walk to Hongu. It sits by the bridge in the middle of the village, near the bus stop.
places.section: Day 2 · Takahara to Chikatsuyu · about 10 km

places.name: Minshuku Chikatsuyu
places.notes: A family-run riverside inn with its own hot spring bath next door and a dining room looking onto the water. Long a walker favorite, so it fills early in peak months.
places.section: Day 2 · Takahara to Chikatsuyu · about 10 km

places.name: Guesthouse SORA Chikatsuyu
places.notes: A homestay with three tatami rooms run by a retired couple, with shared bath and a home-cooked dinner. A quiet alternative to the larger inns.
places.section: Day 2 · Takahara to Chikatsuyu · about 10 km

places.name: CABELO Coffee
places.notes: A tiny roaster in the center of the village with a short menu and good coffee. Open only part of the week, so treat it as a bonus.
places.section: Day 2 · Takahara to Chikatsuyu · about 10 km

places.name: Tsugizakura-oji
places.notes: A ridge-top shrine under enormous old cedars, an hour or two past Chikatsuyu. Take the steps down to Nonaka-no-Shimizu, a spring pilgrims have drunk from for centuries.
places.section: Day 3 · Chikatsuyu to Kumano Hongu Taisha · about 25 km

places.name: Toganoki-jaya Teahouse
places.notes: A thatched teahouse with an open hearth next to Tsugizakura-oji. Sometimes a local volunteer is pouring tea; either way it is a good place to sit for a few minutes.
places.section: Day 3 · Chikatsuyu to Kumano Hongu Taisha · about 25 km

places.name: Kumano Kodo Inn Hagi
places.notes: An old village shop turned into a small inn near Tsugizakura-oji. Staying in Nonaka shortens the long walk to Hongu the next day.
places.section: Day 3 · Chikatsuyu to Kumano Hongu Taisha · about 25 km

places.name: Hosshinmon-oji
places.notes: The gate of awakening, once the outer entrance to Hongu's sacred precinct. Many walkers ride the bus here and walk the last 7 km to Hongu past farms and small oji; check the bus timetable with the Tanabe City Kumano Tourism Bureau.
places.section: Day 3 · Chikatsuyu to Kumano Hongu Taisha · about 25 km

places.name: Fushiogami-oji
places.notes: The viewpoint where tired pilgrims first saw Oyunohara far below and knelt to bow. A teahouse and rest area sit beside it, about an hour above Hongu.
places.section: Day 3 · Chikatsuyu to Kumano Hongu Taisha · about 25 km

places.name: Kumano Hongu Taisha
places.notes: The head shrine of the Kumano faith, reached at the end of the Nakahechi by a stone stairway lined with banners. The cypress-bark roofs and the quiet main courtyard are worth a slow look; stamp your credential at the shrine office.
places.section: Day 4 · Kumano Hongu Taisha and Oyunohara

places.name: Oyunohara
places.notes: The river flat where the shrine stood until an 1889 flood, now a sacred grove behind a giant torii gate. Walk through the rice fields to the gate late in the day, when the crowds are gone.
places.section: Day 4 · Kumano Hongu Taisha and Oyunohara

places.name: Kumano Hongu Heritage Center
places.address: 熊野本宮館, 100-1, Hongucho Hongu, Tanabe, Wakayama, Japan 647-1731
places.notes: A free exhibition hall across the road from the shrine with clear displays on the World Heritage routes, plus restrooms and tourist information in English.
places.section: Day 4 · Kumano Hongu Taisha and Oyunohara

places.name: cafe alma
places.notes: A small coffee stop in the Karasuya building at the foot of the shrine stairs. A good place to sit after arriving, with outdoor tables.
places.section: Day 4 · Kumano Hongu Taisha and Oyunohara

places.name: Blue Sky Guesthouse
places.notes: A small, spotless guesthouse in a side valley of Hongu village, a short walk from both the shrine and Oyunohara. Private rooms and a hearty breakfast; it books out early.
places.section: Day 4 · Kumano Hongu Taisha and Oyunohara

places.name: Dainichi-goe Trail
places.notes: A short, steep forest trail over a ridge between Oyunohara and Yunomine, the way pilgrims went to bathe before visiting the shrine. Allow about 90 minutes and bring a light rain layer.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: Tsuboyu
places.notes: A one-room stone bath in a wooden hut by the creek, the only hot spring bath that is part of a World Heritage site. Take a numbered ticket at the public bath counter and wait your turn; it is private for one or two people.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: J-Hoppers Kumano Yunomine Guesthouse
places.notes: A hostel in an old minshuku with dorm beds and private tatami rooms, plus hot spring baths you can book for yourself. The budget choice in Yunomine.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: Ryokan Adumaya
places.notes: A traditional inn founded by a shrine priest in the 1700s, with wooden baths fed by the village spring and a kaiseki dinner. The splurge night of the trip for many walkers.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: Yoshinoya Ryokan
places.address: よしのや旅館, 173, Hongucho Yunomine, Tanabe, Wakayama, Japan 647-1732
places.notes: A family inn beside Tsuboyu with a private outdoor bath in a small garden and rooms overlooking the creek. Mid-range and well placed for an early soak.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: Kawayu Onsen
places.notes: A riverside village where hot water seeps up through the gravel of the Oto River, so you can dig your own bath on the bank. In winter the town builds a huge open-air pool in the river; check the Kumano Tourism Bureau for dates.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: Fujiya Ryokan
places.notes: One of the larger inns in Kawayu, at the east end of the village facing the river. Guests can borrow a shovel to dig a bath in the gravel bank, which feels like a treat after several nights in small inns.
places.section: Day 5 · Dainichi-goe to Yunomine and Kawayu onsen · about 3.5 km

places.name: Kumano Hayatama Taisha
places.notes: The second of the three grand shrines, bright vermilion against a forested hill near the mouth of the Kumano River. Look for the giant nagi tree in the courtyard and the treasure hall of old offerings.
places.section: Day 6 · Down the Kumano River to Shingu

places.name: Kamikura-jinja
places.notes: A small shrine wedged under a huge boulder high above town, reached by more than 500 rough stone steps. The first stretch is close to a scramble; the view over Shingu and the sea is the reward.
places.section: Day 6 · Down the Kumano River to Shingu

places.name: guesthouse YUZU
places.notes: A restored old house a minute's walk from Hayatama Taisha, with a display of children's portable shrines from the neighborhood festival. A calm base for the coast end of the trip.
places.section: Day 6 · Down the Kumano River to Shingu

places.name: Daimon-zaka
places.notes: A moss-edged stone stairway climbing about 600 m through huge old cedars to the Nachi shrine and temple, starting at the twin Meoto-sugi trees by the bus stop. Go early in the morning to have it mostly to yourself.
places.section: Day 7 · Daimon-zaka to Nachi Falls and Katsuura

places.name: Kumano Nachi Taisha
places.notes: The third grand shrine, high on the mountainside facing the falls, its worship tied to the waterfall itself. Stamp your credential here to complete the three shrines.
places.section: Day 7 · Daimon-zaka to Nachi Falls and Katsuura

places.name: Seiganto-ji
places.notes: A Buddhist temple next door to the shrine and the first stop on the Saigoku Kannon pilgrimage. The three-story vermilion pagoda with Nachi Falls behind it is the view most people come for.
places.section: Day 7 · Daimon-zaka to Nachi Falls and Katsuura

places.name: Nachi Falls
places.address: 〒649-5301, 東牟婁郡那智勝浦町, 那智山1
places.notes: Japan's tallest single-drop waterfall, worshipped as a deity at Hiro-jinja at its base. Walk down the cedar-lined steps from the road for the closest view.
places.section: Day 7 · Daimon-zaka to Nachi Falls and Katsuura

places.name: Katsuura Gyoko Nigiwai Ichiba
places.address: 〒649-5335, 和歌山県東牟婁郡那智勝浦町, 築地7丁目8-2
places.notes: The harbor market in Kii-Katsuura, a major tuna port, with stalls and simple counters serving fresh maguro. A good last meal before the train out.
places.section: Day 7 · Daimon-zaka to Nachi Falls and Katsuura

places.name: Hotel Urashima
places.notes: A sprawling onsen hotel on a peninsula in Katsuura Bay, reached by its own shuttle boat, with cave baths open to the Pacific. Busy and a bit dated, but the baths are memorable.
places.section: Day 7 · Daimon-zaka to Nachi Falls and Katsuura
